planting.note: Plant container plants in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Jade Butterflies is a male, fruitless selection, so it avoids the messy, foul-smelling fruit produced by female ginkgo trees.

directions: Jade Butterflies is a dwarf, shrubby ginkgo selection that stays a densely branched mound only a few feet tall, a striking departure from the towering size of the straight species, with distinctive fan-shaped leaves that are often partly fused or folded, giving them a butterfly-like shape that inspired the cultivar name. Like the species it turns a brilliant, uniform gold in fall, and as a male selection it produces no fruit, avoiding the notoriously foul-smelling seed litter of female ginkgo trees. Extremely tough, pest- and disease-free, and adaptable to poor soil, heat, drought, and urban pollution, it works well as a specimen shrub, foundation planting, or container subject where a full-sized ginkgo tree would be far too large.

common_name: Mary Nell Holly (Upright Pyramidal Glossy Hybrid Holly)

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped hollies in late winter, spring, or fall in well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Mary Nell is a female cultivar, so a male holly blooming at the same time nearby improves berry set, though it often fruits well even without one.

directions: Mary Nell is a vigorous hybrid holly bred for a dense, upright, pyramidal form with glossy, deep green, lightly spined leaves and a heavy fall crop of bright red berries, making it a popular choice for a specimen tree, screen, or formal hedge. It grows faster than many broadleaf evergreens and holds its pyramidal shape with minimal pruning, tolerating Gulf Coast clay soils, heat, and humidity well once established. Give it well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade, and prune, if needed, in late winter or right after the main flush of spring growth to maintain size and shape without removing developing berries.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Evergreen Holly Cultivars
Clemson Cooperative Extension — Holly Selection for Screening

common_name: China Girl Holly (Compact Female Meserve Hybrid Holly)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; China Girl is female and needs a male pollinator such as China Boy planted nearby to set its red berries.

directions: China Girl is a compact, self-branching Meserve hybrid holly with glossy, spiny, dark green leaves and, once pollinated, a reliably heavy crop of bright red winter berries, making it a popular and dependable evergreen shrub for foundation plantings, hedges, and mixed borders. It is more heat-tolerant than some other blue holly selections, an advantage in warmer regions where straight Meserve hollies can struggle, but as a female cultivar it needs a male pollinator such as China Boy blooming nearby to fruit well. Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in full sun to partial shade, and prune, if needed, in late winter before new growth begins.

common_name: China Boy Holly (Compact Male Meserve Hybrid Holly)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; China Boy is the standard male pollinator for China Girl and other female Meserve hollies blooming at the same time, and does not itself produce berries.

directions: China Boy is the male counterpart bred alongside China Girl in the Meserve holly line, sharing the same compact, dense, glossy dark-green, spiny foliage but producing no berries of its own, since only female holly plants fruit. Its main garden role is as a reliable pollinator planted within about 30-40 feet of China Girl or other compatible female Meserve hollies to ensure a heavy berry set on the female plants, though it is also a handsome, fully ornamental evergreen shrub in its own right for a hedge or foundation planting. Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in full sun to partial shade, and prune, if needed, in late winter before new growth begins.

common_name: Blue Maid Holly (Compact Female Meserve Hybrid Blue Holly)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Blue Maid is female and needs a compatible male pollinator such as Blue Prince planted nearby to set its red berries.

directions: Blue Maid carries the blue-green, glossy, spiny foliage typical of the Meserve hybrid hollies on a somewhat more compact plant than Blue Princess, with a dense, well-branched habit suited to a smaller hedge or foundation planting. Once pollinated by a compatible male such as Blue Prince blooming nearby, it produces a heavy crop of bright red berries that persist through winter and provide food for birds. Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in full sun to partial shade, and prune, if needed, in late winter before new spring growth begins, since Meserve hollies generally hold their form well with minimal shaping.
